text: I recognise that to push this in a widespread universal practice across the board is a very huge task and it requires the active participation from all responsible parties in the workforce, not just MOM.

speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (Fengshan)
text: Promoting it and education become the natural first steps in all this raising of awareness.

speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (Fengshan)
text: However, just relying on the influencers or even some of these advocates of like-minded practitioners to push the agenda for fair workplace practices with SMEs and the private sector may take a very long while to materialise.

speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (Fengshan)
text: In an open economy, companies are more susceptible to the dynamics and impact of all the external market forces.

speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (Fengshan)
text: Increasingly, we have observed that trends and all these indicators reflect our workplace as one where it is commonly seen with frequent company restructuring, reduction in breadth of our industries, earlier retirement of our skilled workers and difficulty in well-educated mature workers being re-employed.

speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (Fengshan)
text: Over time, these trends are invariably more challenging to deal with.

speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (Fengshan)
text: I feel one area to look into urgently is that of the employment agencies, particularly those that are outsourced.

speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (Fengshan)
text: These HR firms actually have very short-term commitments and also non-contractual commitments to the employees who are being hired on behalf of the hiring companies.

speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (Fengshan)
text: The parties impacted would be the freelancers, part-timers and mature workers.

speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (Fengshan)
text: For those who have to make career switches due to market conditions or with their acquired upskills through their lifelong learning, it will be beneficial for them to have better visibility and understanding of practices in the new industries before they venture into them.

speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (Fengshan)
text: Awareness and rolling out these good practices would only more effectively circumvent the need for extensive mediation in the long run.

speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (Fengshan)
text: Hopefully, through all these different support networks, our vulnerable working groups and PMEs could improve their job opportunities and achieve fair work packages.

speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
text: Deputy Speaker, I support the Bill, which will provide for the expeditious resolution of salary-related disputes through the ECT.

speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
text: However, I hope that they will be included soon to ensure universal access and reduce confusion and duplication.

speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
text: Workers will still have to pursue these claims through MOM, if they are covered under the EA, or through the civil Courts, which can be costly.

speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
text: (In Mandarin):   Recently, one of my residents approached me for help as his employer in the marine engineering sector had been cutting his pay repeatedly to force him to quit.

speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
text: There are also employers who place unreasonable demands on their workers or practise psychological warfare to pressure them to resign.

speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
text: Most employees cannot afford the legal fees to prove their cases and seek compensation for such maltreatment.

speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
text: Employers are aware of this and some exploit their workers in the knowledge that they will not be held accountable.

speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
text: Illiterate, mentally and physically disabled and elderly employees are particularly vulnerable.

speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
text: I urge MOM to look into this loophole and close it for better protection of our workers.

speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
text: Having a dedicated tribunal which can investigate and mediate will provide more assurance for our workers.

speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
text: It would be necessary to put a cap on the legal fees or provide legal aid so that suffering workers will not be deterred from making legitimate complaints.

speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
text: (In English): Next, I would like to ask what happens if the employer has filed to wind up the company or if the proprietor or partners have been declared bankrupt.

speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
text: In such scenarios, there will be a limitation as to how much the tribunal can help the employees.

speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
text: However, once the claimant has abandoned the excess amount, he cannot recover that amount in a tribunal or any other Court.

speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
text: I think that the claimant should be given the option to pursue the excess subsequently, even those within a limited time frame.

speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
text: We must understand that most of our population are working people with immediate financial needs to meet – children to feed, education, medical fees, mortgage and instalment payments, parents to support and so on.

speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
text: Page: 102 The expeditious recovery of salaries due is to minimise hardships to the claimants and their dependants.

speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
text: When the claimant's situation is stabilised later, he should have the chance to recover any additional funds.

speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
text: He should not be penalised for choosing a quick interim solution to reduce the negative impact on his family.

speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
text: Can such cases be adjudicated through this tribunal?

speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
text: Before I respond to them to the best of my ability, let me just set the stage first, and take a step back.

speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
text: In the Second Reading opening this speech, I highlighted that, right now, there are three avenues for workers to settle their dispute with their employers – by becoming a union member, through the Labour Court as well as through the civil Court.

speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
text: We are not trying to find one solution to replace all three because each one, on its own, serves a very important purpose.

speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
text: For example, unions must continue to be allowed to play a very important role because if the day were to come where our legal framework becomes so comprehensive that unions no longer have a role to play, eventually the Labour Movement will become weak.

speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
text: When the Labour Movement becomes weak, the day will come when the workers can no longer be protected adequately in all aspects of work.

speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
text: Just look at what is happening in the US today.

speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
text: The labour movement is weak; everybody recognises it.

speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
text: In recent years, we have heard many public reports lamenting that the weakness of the labour movement in the US is today a major weakness in their labour landscape.

speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
text: But in the case of the US, will they be able to find a way for the labour movement to be strong again?

speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
text: This is something for them to worry about, to think about.

speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
text: In Singapore, the Labour Movement is strong, it is healthy.

speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
text: Therefore, let me stress, firstly, that it is not our intention to weaken the role of the unions through the ECT.

speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
text: The ECT is meant to be a cheaper, better, faster way of resolving disputes.

speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
text: Cheaper – must be highly affordable, more so than the civil Courts.

speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
text: Better – because it must be able to help more and more employees, including those not covered by EA, to have access to the ECT.

speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
text: Lastly, faster – we want the disputes to be resolved as quickly as possible.

speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
text: Against that backdrop, let me start by saying that I know many of you will be disappointed by my response, but please bear in mind this.

speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
text: I think Member Mr Dennis Tan or Assoc Prof Daniel Goh said that the ECT is a good start.

speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
text: We want to have a good start to the ECT and this good start need not be the ending point, it is just a good start.

speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
text: Against that backdrop, let me try to respond to some of the specific points.

speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
text: Page: 103 First, Mr Patrick Tay asked about apprentices and interns who are under contracts of service.

speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
text: Mr Patrick Tay and Mr Zainal Sapari talked about frivolous claims.

speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
text: So, even $50 can be a valid claim.

speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
text: Mr Zainal Sapari asked whether employees filing for CPF claims can come under the ECT.

speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
text: Workers do not have to claim for non-payment of CPF.

speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
text: All they need to do is notify CPF and we will take enforcement action on their behalf.

speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
text: Mr Faisal Manap and Mr Dennis Tan asked why not include foreign domestic workers.

speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
text: We have mentioned it before that foreign domestic workers and other categories of workers already have access to separate mechanisms today.

speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
text: Today, their claims are not under the Labour Court.

speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
text: Based on our experience with the Labour Court, six months and one year would be sufficient to cater for most cases.

speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
text: But one important point is that based on our experience with the Labour Court, evidence becomes harder to gather, harder to collate, as the time passed by.

speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
text: As a result, we believe that by imposing this time limit, it will actually force both employers and employees to take quick action.

speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
text: If you have a claim, make it quickly, why wait?

speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
text: And bear in mind, there is a limit of $20,000, $30,000.

speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
text: The longer the workers wait to file their claims, the more the workers accumulate their claims, the more likely they are going to be affected by the claim limit.

speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
text: So, I would say that having a faster claim works to the advantage of the workers.

speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
text: If I set it at $50,000, Members will ask why $50,000?

speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
text: If I say $100,000, Members will ask why $100,000?

speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
text: Today, at the Labour Court, we have a $20,000 limit for PMEs; for the rank-and-file, there is no limit.

speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
text: But we discovered that, for the rank-and-file, $20,000 is more than adequate.

speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
text: As a result, we decided to continue the existing claim limit of the Labour Court.

speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
text: But this number is not cast in concrete.

speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
text: We will review it from time to time through tripartite consultation.

speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
text: Mr Gan Thiam Poh asked why the claimants cannot recover their abandoned claim amounts in other Courts.

speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
text: This is to avoid multiple proceedings in different Courts and tribunals over the same dispute.

speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
text: This is in line with the State Courts' existing practice.

speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
text: It is not something new to the ECT.

speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
text: Mr Zainal Sapari asked about the timeframe for mediation sessions.

speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
text: We will continue with this best practice under the ECT.

speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
text: Mr Murali Pillai asked whether new claims that may arise between mediation and ECT hearings can be combined.

speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
text: The answer is yes, we will consider his suggestion.

speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
text: However, I would prefer to limit it to only similar and related claims because, if the claims are completely different, it is better that they go through mediation.

speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
text: Because if we allow legal representation, it is more likely that the employer will be able to afford legal representation, compared to the employee.

speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
text: But, more importantly, as I have mentioned, we want the ECT to be a very affordable, very expeditious way of resolving disputes.

speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
text: Any complex cases that require legal representation, they should go to the civil Court rather than come to the ECT.

speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
text: We are not saying that this is not important; we are just saying that it is outside the scope of the ECT.

speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
text: Union members in a non-unionised company, who undergo the TMF, can seek consent from ECT for their tripartite mediation advisors to observe their ECT hearings.

speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
text: These will be prescribed in the subsidiary legislation, in black and white.

speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
text: Mr Zainal Sapari asked whether the next-of-kin (NOK) can make the claim for some members.

speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
text: Generally speaking, claimants must make their claims in person.

speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
text: But in cases where the employee does not have the capacity to represent himself, his NOK may apply to the Courts to be appointed as a deputy under the Mental Capacity Act.

speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
text: Once appointed as a deputy, the NOK may then submit a mediation request on behalf of the employee.

speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
text: Some Members also expressed the concern on what if the worker is not able to express himself, not able to present his case fairly due to whatever constraint, then whether the judgment will be a fair one.

speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
text: Here, I want to assure the Members that the tribunal magistrates appointed to the ECT will be legally qualified and they will decide on each case, its merits, and in accordance with the relevant legislation, case law and legal principles.

speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
text: So, the judge will lead the tribunal and may allow individuals with relevant skills and experience to act as assessors, as suggested by Mr Murali Pillai.

speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
text: The ECT may also summon any person to give evidence or produce relevant documents.

speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
text: Parties may appeal to the High Court against an ECT order on grounds of law and jurisdiction.

speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
text: In other words, all these measures are to ensure that there will be a fair outcome.

speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
text: In terms of the processing of ECT cases, I would like to assure Mr Patrick Tay that the ECT and TADM will continue to prioritise the urgent cases, which is what we are doing in the Labour Court today.

speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
text: I agree with Mr Patrick Tay that the claim process should be simplified where possible.

speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
text: At the same time, Mr Zainal Sapari also asked about the ECT's operating hours and having some claim forms in the vernacular languages.

speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
text: The ECT will align its processes with those of the other State Court tribunals.

speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
text: MOM will work with the State Courts to customise the services of the ECT according to the needs of the workers.

speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
text: Mr Louis Ng had some questions regarding ECT records and grounds of decisions.

speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
text: MOM and the State Courts will explore these matters in the drafting of the subsidiary legislation.

speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
text: On ECT fees, Mr Patrick Tay, Mr Louis Ng and some other Members touched on the affordability of ECT fees.

speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
text: I fully agree that the fees should be kept affordable.

speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
text: In fact, that is the whole purpose of the ECT.

speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
text: We will consider various suggestions, for example, to tier fees by claim amounts and so on.

speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
text: Ms Thanaletchimi asked how the ECT orders can be enforced.

speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
text: If the orders are not complied with, they can commence debt recovery by applying to the State Courts for a Writ of Seizure and Sales.

speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
text: I think Members are concerned about what if the workers do not know how to go about doing this, and whether it will be too costly for them.

speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
text: TADM will give them advice and assist them to go through that process.

speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
text: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh referred to my reply to a Parliamentary Question on 11 May 2015, mentioning that of those employers who did not comply with the Labour Court's orders, 80% of them turned out to be able to pay.

speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
text: Maybe the way I put it was not so clear.

speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
text: Only 20% did not make the full payment.

speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
text: Of those 20% who were unable to make full payment, the majority of them were due to financial difficulties, in some cases, going out of business.

speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
text: For those who wilfully disobey the Labour Court orders, they can be prosecuted under the EA or salary offences.

speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
text: So, we do have the mechanism to prosecute them.

speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
text: We have done so and will continue to do so.

speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
text: To help the local vulnerable workers who are caught in situations where companies may not have assets to be seized or may have stopped operations and are unable to make the payment, Assoc Prof Daniel Goh, Mr Louis Ng, Miss Cheryl Chan, Mr Gan Thiam Poh and other Members asked whether we can do something to help them.

speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
text: On public communication, I agree with Members Mr Patrick Tay and Mr Zainal Sapari that it is important to raise awareness about the ECT and TADM, including the rules and processes.

speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
text: So, MOM certainly will work with the tripartite partners and key stakeholders to do so.

speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
text: I also agree with Mr Thomas Chua who highlighted that it is important for the employers, especially SMEs, to enhance and raise their HR competencies so as to avoid disputes rather than to be faced with disputes.

speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
text: We will do our part as well to help to upgrade the HR capabilities amongst SMEs.

speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
text: Mr Murali Pillai asked what kind of claims will continue to come to the Commissioner for Labour under the EA .

speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
text: Mr Murali Pillai asked why is it that employers should raise the issue of re-employment eligibility during mediation and not during the ECT hearing.

speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
text: I want to clarify that under the RRA, re-employment eligibility is determined by MOM.

speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
text: If the employees and the employers have 	Page: 106 disagreements over re-employment eligibility, the employee should come to MOM and we will get it settled.

speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
text: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh asked about the outcomes of public consultation conducted earlier this year.

speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
text: We did receive feedback, and many of the feedback were similar to the issues raised by the Members today.

speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
text: A summary of the feedback and the response will be made available online on the Reaching Everyone for Active Citizenry @ Home (REACH) platform following the debate in this House.

speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
text: For example, Mr Patrick Tay asked about reviewing our employment legislation.

speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
text: Over the years, we have progressively expanded our EA coverage for PMEs.

speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
text: We first extended salary protection under the EA to PMEs earning less than $2,500 because, prior to that, there was no coverage for PMEs.

speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
text: In 2008, we included PMEs earning less than $2,500 under our EA.

speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
text: This salary ceiling was raised to $4,500 in 2011.

speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
text: In 2014, we amended the EA to give PMEs some non-salary protection, such as sick leave benefits, unfair dismissal.

speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
text: We will continue to work with the tripartite partners to regularly review our employment legislation, including the EA salary ceiling as suggested by Mr Patrick Tay.

speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
text: Mr Tay also asked about covering more types of disputes under the TMF.

speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
text: Today's Bill now allows the TMF to cover a broader range of disputes, including salary-related and non-salary related disputes, like re-employment.

speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
text: We will continue our discussions with the tripartite partners for the TMF to cover more non salary-related disputes, such as unfair dismissal.

speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
text: This is something we will do through tripartite consultation.

speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
text: Mr Faisal Manap, Mr Dennis Tan, Ms K Thanaletchimi and Mr Gan Thiam Poh also asked whether the ECT could hear non salary-related disputes in future, including unfair dismissals, workplace injury claims, discrimination and so on.

speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
text: The tripartite partners will continue to deliberate on this issue.

speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
text: At the end of the day, what we really want to strive for is having good progressive HR practices at the workplaces so that disputes can be prevented.

speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
text: The ECT is a solution to resolving disputes.

speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
text: However, we must not forget that, at the end of the day, avoidance of disputes is better than resolving disputes.

speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
text: I also agree with Mr Thomas Chua's point about paying more attention in supporting SMEs.

speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
text: We will be doing even more to help SMEs to keep upgrading their HR capability.

speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
text: I share Mr Thomas Chua's concern that if the ECT mechanism is made too complicated, many SMEs may not be able to cope with it.

speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
text: That is the reason why we have set up the ECT as a first step to be as simple and direct as possible.

speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
text: Page: 107 I believe that the establishment of the ECT and TADM is an important step forward in addressing salary-related claims for all workers and, hopefully, will create a more comprehensive dispute management landscape here and lay the foundation for us to continue to update and evolve the dispute resolution mechanism in Singapore.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai
text: I have one short clarification to make in relation to his answer about a claim under the RRA.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai
text: The Minister mentioned that the employment eligibility criteria are set by the Ministry.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai
text: The thrust of my question is not that.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai
text: It is in relation to the fact that the defence of the employer can only be raised if the employer had raised it in the course of mediation.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai
text: The problem with that is that mediation is usually seen as a "without prejudice" kind of a discussion where there is a certain level of candour expected.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai
text: Perhaps, as a halfway point, one way to deal with this issue is to provide, under the regulations, that the employer would be raising this defence on a headline basis that the employee did not satisfy the criteria, without really going into the facts and details so that it is highlighted at the mediation stage and, later on, if it proceeds to the tribunal stage, the tribunal can take cognisance of whether or not the employer had declared that this would be a defence to the employee's claim.

speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
text: So, at the mediation stage, if the employer feels that the employee is not eligible for re-employment, that is where he should bring it up during the mediation.

speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
text: And if the mediator agrees with the employer that the employee does not qualify for re-employment, the case is closed.

speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
text: Once MOM rules that the person is eligible for re-employment, then the mediation will proceed.

speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
text: After the mediation, if there is no outcome, they will go to the ECT.

speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
text: That is my understanding of how it works.

speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
text: So, by the time it goes to the ECT to re-debate on the eligibility of the employee, it is, in a way, setting back the whole process all over again.

speaker: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong
text: I have a minor clarification for the Minister on the "80%, 20%" point.

speaker: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong
text: I am quoting the Minister from the Hansard: "At the same time, employers were also taken to the Labour Court to settle the payments to the workers.

speaker: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong
text: For that, last year (2014), we cleared about 1,630 cases.

speaker: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong
text: And of these cases, two-thirds of the workers were able to receive full payment.

speaker: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong
text: However, one-third of them, due to financial difficulties faced by the companies, received either partial payment or no payment.

speaker: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong
text: We investigated further into those employers who were not 	Page: 108 able to make full payment and we discovered that 80% of the employers were able to make full payment but 20% of them were unable to pay due to financial difficulties." So, it seems that of the one-third that initially did not pay to the workers to settle the claims, 80% were found to be able to make the full payment because of MOM's investigation.

speaker: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong
text: My questions are: did MOM actively then enforce the order on this 80% and get them to make the full payment to the workers?

speaker: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong
text: Would MOM then continue to do so for the ECT?

speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
text: I read the Hansard as well and I think the way I worded it may have created this wrong impression.

speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
text: This is the reason why I thought it is important that I clarify it here.

speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
text: Of the 20% that did not make full payment, some of them did not have assets for seizure, some of them had run into financial difficulties or they had closed down their businesses.

speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
text: For those who are able to make payment, but for whatever reason refuse to make payment, we prosecute them under the EA because this is a salary offence.

speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
text: In other words, even with the ECT, we still have the right to pursue employers for failing to make salary payments.

speaker: Ms K Thanaletchimi
text: Section 10 of the Bill seems to be silent on the contents of the record of the tribunal and whether parties are entitled to a copy of the records.

speaker: Ms K Thanaletchimi
text: Will the decision of the ECT be made available to the parties in written form?

speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
text: For example, whether the issue of re-employment eligibility was discussed in mediation, the information will be made available to the ECT.

speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
text: Likewise, the records of the ECT, as I had replied earlier to the suggestions made by Mr Louis Ng, we will work together with the State Courts to look into these proposals.

speaker: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong
text: The Minister said that MOM will continue to prosecute those who do not want to pay under the EA.

speaker: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong
text: But would this cover PMEs because the EA does not cover PMEs?

speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
text: By the way, for TMF, that is, likewise, the biggest improvement.

speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
text: Salary-related settlement agreements at TMF are now enforceable through registration with the District Courts.
